title: The Missourians' personnel and sound
summary: He describes the Missourians as three brass, three saxes and rhythm with tuba player Smitty and trumpet soloist R.Q. Dickerson; Benny Carter arrangements were brought in.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Right. So now, they got me in the band, and the first thing I started to doing was started getting them to write something. Then I think we eventually got Benny Carter to do arrangements for us...
See, now, the Missourians was a good band.
Oh, you got in the Missourians now.
They didn't have but three brass, three saxophones, and I guess they had four rhythm, because they had a bass upright... They didn't have no kind of bass; we had that band bass...
I guess his name was Smith, but all they called him was Smitty. I never knew his right name. I remember the trumpet player, R.Q. Dickerson. R.Q. played good.
And Lamar didn't play... He played a little Jazz, but he didn't play much.
